title: Agentic Algorithm Design: LLMs that Propose, Formalise, and Prove Runtime Bounds for Evolutionary Algorithms in Lean
title_zh: 智能体化算法设计：在Lean中提出、形式化并证明演化算法运行时间边界的LLM

paragraphs.en: 提出分阶段智能体流水线，在Lean中设计黑盒优化算法并机器检查其期望运行时间边界。 LLMs now prove hard theorems in Lean. Can they also design algorithms and prove their correctness and efficiency? LLM-guided design of optimisation heuristics (such as AlphaEvolve) is purely empirical. Automated theorem provers with LLMs prove given statements. So far, there has been little evidence that LLMs can do both: design an algorithm and guarantee its efficiency by a mathematical proof. We present a staged pipeline modelled after research methodology in design and analysis of evolutionary algorithms. The agent proposes black-box optimisation algorithms, and Lean guards filter out flawed designs. The agent then defines a potential function and proves drift bounds that guarantee an expected runtime improvement over the baseline algorithm. At no point in the pipeline are the algorithms compared empirically. The agent generates a black-box optimisation algorithm with expected runtime $O(n^2)$ on a CycleUncover problem, where the classical (1+1) EA needs runtime $e^{Ω(n)}$. The pipeline also designs and analyses a black-box optimisation algorithm for integer-valued submodular minimisation with expected runtime $O(n^{2+2c})$, and it matches the optimal order $O(n^2)$ on LeadingOnes. Across 8 problem classes, 12 of 15 runs with frontier models complete the pipeline with a machine-checked expected-runtime bound. An ablation study shows that removing the staging and asking the agent to zero-shot an algorithmic design with a runtime guarantee leads to a copy of the seeded baseline algorithm (random search) or to incomplete proofs. Our study suggests that machine-checked specifications in Lean can replace empirical evaluation in open-ended algorithm discovery. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of an automated pipeline that designs efficient black-box optimisation algorithms with machine-checked runtime bounds in Lean.
paragraphs.zh: 提出一种分阶段的智能体流水线，在Lean中设计黑盒优化算法并对其期望运行时间边界进行机器检查。大语言模型如今已能在Lean中证明困难的定理。 它们是否也能设计算法并证明其正确性与有效性？ 由大语言模型引导的优化启发式算法设计（如AlphaEvolve）纯粹是经验性的。 结合大语言模型的自动定理证明器可以证明给定的命题。 迄今为止，几乎没有证据表明大语言模型能够同时做到这两点：设计一个算法并通过数学证明保证其有效性。 我们提出一种分阶段流水线，其建模仿照了进化算法设计与分析中的研究方法论。 智能体提出黑盒优化算法，而Lean守卫会过滤掉有缺陷的设计。 随后，智能体定义一个势函数并证明漂移边界，从而保证相对于基线算法的期望运行时间改进。 在整个流水线中，任何环节都不对算法进行经验性比较。 智能体生成了一个黑盒优化算法，在CycleUncover问题上的期望运行时间为 $O(n^2)$，而经典的 (1+1) EA 需要 $e^{Ω(n)}$ 的运行时间。 该流水线还为整数 valued 的次模最小化设计并分析了期望运行时间为 $O(n^{2+2c})$ 的黑盒优化算法，并且在LeadingOnes上达到最优阶 $O(n^2)$。 在8个问题类别上，使用前沿模型的15次运行中有12次完成了整个流水线，并得到机器检查的期望运行时间边界。 一项消融实验表明，如果去掉分阶段设置，直接要求智能体零样本地完成带运行时间保证的算法设计，其结果是复制种子基线算法（随机搜索）或给出不完整的证明。 我们的研究表明，Lean中机器检查的规约可以在开放式算法发现中取代经验性评估。 据我们所知，这是首个在Lean中设计高效黑盒优化算法并给出机器检查运行时间边界的自动化流水线实例。
